neighbours.label: an additive or equative focus construction that adds a second item on equal footing (as well as, so too, any more than), versus 'well' as an adverb and plain comparisons
fire: The museum shows paintings as well as old maps of the region.
Our neighbor was a farmer as well as a part-time preacher in the valley.
The program helps adults as well as teenagers who want to learn to read.
In the north, so too, did the price of bread rise that winter.
The rain soaked the tents as well as everything stored inside them.
She could not stay angry at him, any more than she could stop loving him.
This soup is good for colds as well as for upset stomachs.
His sister speaks French as well as some Italian from her years abroad.
quiet: The museum shows paintings and, upstairs, old maps of the region.
Our neighbor was a farmer and later a preacher in the valley.
The program helps adults who read well but want to write better.
In the north, the price of bread rose sharply that winter.
The rain soaked the tents, and the wind knocked them down.
She could not stay angry at him, since he had said he was sorry.
This soup tastes good and keeps well in the fridge.
His sister speaks French as fast as a native speaker from Lyon.
